Hi Alice / Zettle ops team,

We wanted to let you know about a planned maintenance window in the Westus3 region next week: a coordinated kernel + NIC driver rollforward that affects a subset of inference-serving hosts. Expected window (UTC): 2027-11-15 02:00–05:00 (Westus3 local: 2027-11-14 18:00–21:00 PST).

Summary of impact:
- Scope: ~18% of shared GPU pool in westus3 will be cycled in 10–12 minute staggered batches.
- Customer-visible: brief connection re-establishments during node drain (typical tail spikes up to ~200–300ms for in-flight requests). We do not expect request failures for requests under 30s; we will drain inflight tokens and preserve KV cache where possible.
- Dedicated customers: if you are on a Dedicated cluster (reserved pool), you will be routed to your isolated capacity and should not see rolling restarts. If you have questions about your tenancy, tell us and we'll confirm.

What we will do:
- Maintain graceful drains, KV cache snapshotting for eligible models, and continue rolling back automatically if kernel boot fails health checks.
- Keep a read-only fallback (compatible model variant) available in a neighboring AZ if we detect degraded throughput.
- Stream status updates to the status page and via the webhook you already configured.

Action requested from Zettle:
1) Reply to confirm the 2027-11-15 UTC window is acceptable.
2) Provide an operations contact + phone number we can call on-call during the window.
3) If you run pinned model versions, tell us the model id(s) so we can validate compatibility with the new driver ahead of the window.

Attached: westus3-maintenance-checklist.pdf (customer-facing checklist), customer-swagger-compat-matrix.xlsx (model compatibility matrix).

If helpful I can schedule a 30-minute pre-flight call this week to walk the runbook.

Thanks,

Hi Alice — great questions, answers below: 

1) KV cache & streaming sessions:
- For streaming/chat we will preserve hot KV entries during the graceful drain for any session that has activity in the last 5 minutes. Long-running sessions with large KV footprints may see a rewarm penalty on first request after failover — typically a few hundred ms. We will not intentionally evict customer KV during the operation.

2) Expected latency delta:
- Typical baseline: 95th percentile unchanged; 99th percentile tail can move by 150–400ms during the short reconnect window for affected nodes. In our internal simulations for similar rollforwards the 99th spike lasted < 3 minutes per micro-batch. We plan to stage batches to keep customer-visible impact distributed.

3) Routing/rollback behavior:
- If health checks fail in a batch, automatic rollback is triggered for that rack. For catastrophic failures we will route to an advertised compatible variant in a nearby region (eastus2) for read-only workloads. We will only do cross-region routing with your permission — confirm if you'd like us to enable automatic cross-region fallback.

Pre-flight call: Thursday 2027-11-11 10:00 PT works for us. I'll send a calendar invite with the runbook link and the checklist attached.

Escalation contact during window: Redwood on-call +1 (888) 900-REWD (option 2) and engineering lead Grace O'Connor (grace_oconnor@redwood.ai).

I attached the checklist and the compatibility matrix to this message for your infra team to review.

Best,
Ben
